slides.title: Letters, sounds and first reading
slides.slide: L1 Basic · Letters, sounds and first reading
slides.notes: Match letters to sounds and read short words and simple sentences aloud. Notes: use the sounds s, a, t, p, i, n; learners blend them into sat, pin and tap, then read a three-word sentence and clap the syllables.

slides.title: Sentences and simple writing
slides.slide: L2 Awareness · Sentences and simple writing
slides.notes: Write a clear sentence with a capital letter and full stop, and read a short story with understanding. Notes: give a picture prompt; learners say the sentence first, write it, and check capital, spacing and full stop with a partner before reading it aloud.

slides.title: Paragraphs, grammar and reading for meaning
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Paragraphs, grammar and reading for meaning
slides.notes: Write a paragraph of five connected sentences and identify nouns, verbs and adjectives in a text. Notes: colour nouns blue and verbs red in a short passage; learners then write about their street, using at least two adjectives and one linking word.

slides.title: Essays, speaking and responding to texts
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Essays, speaking and responding to texts
slides.notes: Write a 300-word structured essay and give a short talk, quoting evidence from a text to support a view. Notes: model Point, Evidence, Explain; learners write one paragraph about a character, quote one line, and explain what it shows, then speak it aloud.

slides.title: Analysis, argument and style
slides.slide: L5 Specialist · Analysis, argument and style
slides.notes: Analyse a writer's choices of language and structure and write a sustained argument of 600 words. Notes: take two openings of different short stories; learners compare tone, sentence length and imagery in a table, then argue which opening works better and why.

slides.title: Literary and linguistic study
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Literary and linguistic study
slides.notes: Evaluate texts through a critical lens, tracing how language changes across time and context in a researched essay. Notes: compare an older and a modern passage; learners list five differences in vocabulary and syntax and argue in 1,500 words what each reveals about its period.

slides.title: Research, editing and authorship
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Research, editing and authorship
slides.notes: Produce an original piece of research or a polished long-form text, with a literature review and defended method. Notes: pick a narrow question about language in one genre; build a corpus of fifty samples, analyse patterns, write 5,000 words, and revise after external review.
